candidate.educational_objective: Interpret HCAHPS as a standardized patient-experience survey rather than a direct clinical-outcome, staff-satisfaction, or billing measure.

options.A: Treat HCAHPS as a direct measure of clinical outcomes such as mortality, readmissions, and complication rates rather than as a survey of the patient’s hospital experience.
options.B: Use HCAHPS to evaluate standardized patient-reported experience domains such as communication, staff responsiveness, care coordination, environment, discharge information, and overall hospital rating.
options.C: Interpret HCAHPS as a staff-satisfaction instrument because its primary purpose is to compare nurse and physician perceptions of workload and leadership across hospitals.
options.D: Use HCAHPS mainly to evaluate billing accuracy and insurance processing because financial experience is the principal domain used for public comparison of acute-care hospitals.

candidate.rationale: CMS describes HCAHPS as a national, standardized, publicly reported survey of patients’ perspectives of hospital care. Current survey domains include communication, responsiveness, care coordination, environment, discharge information, medication communication, and overall rating/recommendation. It is not a direct mortality/readmission metric, staff-satisfaction instrument, or billing survey.
candidate.source_claim_supported: HCAHPS is the standardized national patient-experience survey for hospitals and reports defined patient-experience domains.
candidate.source_locator: CMS HCAHPS Overview/About the Survey and current survey-measure domains.
candidate.source_version_date: Current CMS HCAHPS program and 2025 survey/content updates rechecked 2026-08-16.
candidate.stem: A quality-improvement committee reviews its hospital’s HCAHPS results. Which interpretation of the survey is most accurate?
